 Nitish Parth Sarthi & Chandana Kumari, Ac to Addl.S.G.I.

Oral Order
10 / Dated : 21.06.2023
1.

Apprehending his arrest, petitioner- Rakesh Kumar Srivastava has moved this Court for grant of
privilege of anticipatory bail in connection with Rc 0932017(S) 0083/Cbi Eo-6, Ranchi, 2017
(Nagar P.S. Giridih and Fir No. 68/2015) registered under Sections 406, 420, 467, 468, 471, 34,
120B of Indian Penal Code, pending in the court of SDJM-cum-Special J.M., Cbi, Dhanbad.

2. As per the prosecution case, two FIRs being Sector-IV Bokaro P.S. Case No. 68 of 2015 and Nagar
Giridih P.S. Case No. 67 of 2016 were registered on the basis of written report lodged by the private
complainant under Sections 406, 420, 467, 468, 471, 120B, 34 of Ipc.
3.

The investigation in this case was taken over by the CBI in compliance to the order of this Court passed in W.P.(PIL) No. 1635 of 2014 dated 21.04.2017 and W.P.(PIL) No. 642 of 2016 dated 3.4.2015.
4.

After investigation charge sheet has been submitted being charge sheet no.03/2020, under Sections 120 B r/w 420 of IPC and Sections 4,5 &6 r/s Section 3 of Prize, Chits & Money Circulation Rakesh Kumar Srivastava vs The State Of Jharkhand on 21 June, 2023

Schemes (Banning) Act, 1978 against this petitioner and others on 30.06.2020.

5. As per the prosecution case, the accused persons collected Rs 7.02 lakhs from Jay Prakash Mishra of Bokaro and total amount of Rs.1.5 Crore from Mehtab Alam and investors of Giridih, by promising them hefty interest/returns in short time on the pretext of making investments in the schemes of the Company.

Sarda Pleasure and Adventure Ltd on the pretext of making investment in the scheme of the company like redeemable preference share (fixed deposit scheme), recurring deposit scheme (RD Scheme), monthly investment scheme (MIS) during the period from 2011 to 2014.
Rakesh Kumar Srivastava was the main director of the accused company along with other directors.

Another company was incorporated in the name of M/s Sarada Mutual Benefit (Nidhi)
Ltd. on 29.05.2008 and 28.02.2013 respectively for unauthorized collection of money from public in the bogus schemes floated by the accused company.
6. The petitioner is charged to have organized meeting with the agents as well as the investors inviting investments in the fraudulent schemes.
This petitioner in order to lure the investors advertised different investment schemes on behalf of M/s
Sarada
Mutual Benefit (Nidhi) Ltd. in which he assured interest range from 10% to 32%
. It is further case of the prosecution that these investment companies were not authorized by the RBI to raise investment and they have violated the SEBI guidelines while raising investments.
In the process, 629 investors have been duped who invested of Rs.2,43,63,700/- in fixed deposit scheme.
Further investments were invited.
In this manner, for different scheme the company raised investments of Rs. 9,21,77,322/- from 1030 investors.
The petitioner has signed the certificate of investment made by the public.
7. Further, case has been unfolded in the supplementary charge sheet filed on behalf of the CBI on 30.03.2022.
Modus operandi was involved in keeping the dummy director in the company.
The petitioner has opened account in IDBI Bank Ltd., Bokaro and has credited Rs. 11,92,14,934/- and out of which withdrawal for a sum of Rs. 6,60,57,925/- was encashed.
It has come that the amounts were encashed by the employees and handed over to the petitioner.
Total cash withdrawal of Rs.3,95,64,809/- from different accounts of the company was allegedly made by this petitioner through his employees.
8. It is submitted by learned counsel for the petitioner that the name of the company did not figure in the order passed by this Court in W.P.(PIL) No. 1635 of 2014.

It is further submitted that the FIR has been lodged by the CBI against the company consequent to the order passed in W.P.(PIL) No.
4092 of 2014 which has been filed by none other than the General Secretary of Sarda Pleasure and Adventure Ltd. and M/s Sarda Mutual Benefit (Nidhi) Ltd.
As a matter of fact, it was this petitioner who had embezzled huge sum of the company to the tune of more than Rs.5 Crore.

It is further submitted that the company was not a non-banking company rather it will be apparent on the memorandum of association of Sarda Pleasure and Adventure Ltd. that the main object was to carry on in India or elsewhere the business of contractors, turnkey contractor etc. for which to operate in this field RBI concurrence/permission was not required.
It was a public limited company and under Section 53 of the Companies Act it could issue shares which are redeemable.

During investigation,
the petitioner was not apprehended and charge sheet has already been submitted and the petitioner is ready to face the trial.

sentences.text: In both the cases, the petitioner has been enlarged on bail after submission of charge sheet.
10. It is further submitted that after investigation charge sheet has been submitted and during the investigation, at no point of time, custody of this petitioner was sought by the C.B.I.
Throughout the investigation, this petitioner had co-operated with the investigation.
It is further submitted that the complainant Mahtab Alam, on whose complaint, present case has been registered have appeared before this Court by filing Vakalatnama.

It is submitted that Ambuj Kumar Singh and Mahtab Alam were the main agents of the Company, who collected huge investments from the investors and after misappropriating the amount, they have lodged the case.

There are documentary evidence to the effect that both the opposite party nos.2 and 4 had received the amount running into Crores from the petitioner and therefore, their statement that they have been defrauded, is far from truth and is on false affidavit for which the petitioner contemplates to file appropriate petition under Section 340 of the Cr.P.C.
11.

Learned counsel appearing for the CBI has opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that the present case has been registered pursuant to the direction of this Court passed in writ petitions and two specific cases were taken, Bokaro Sector IV P.S. Case No.68 of 2015 lodged by Jai Prakash Mishra and Nagar Giridih P.S. Case No.67 of 2016 dated 26.03.2016 lodged by Mahtab Alam.
On investigation, it was found that the main related Company had received Rs.9,21,77,322/- from 1030 investors, out of this amount which was received from the investors.
It is further submitted that in the supplementary charge sheet, final investment has been computed to the tune of Rs.11,92,14,934/-.
Out of said investment, Rs.6,60,57,925/- were the cash withdrawals.
This amount was misappropriated by the petitioner for his personal use.
The modus has come-up that he used to give cheque to his employees and for the withdrawal of cash from the bank account.
It is also submitted that these amounts were found during investigation raised from State of Jharkhand.

It is also submitted that the person from whom cash was withdrawn, have gone on record during investigation of State that the amount was withdrawn under the instruction of this petitioner and given to him.
It has come in the investigation that 101 debenture redeemed, signed by this petitioner, was seized during investigation wherein the amount has not been repaid.
The details have been mentioned at Annexure-2 to the first charge sheet.
12. It is submitted by Mr. Mukesh Kumar, learned counsel for opposite party no.2, that it was on his petition that this Court had directed C.B.I. investigation in the case.
He had served as an agent in the Company.
Initially, he was an investor, later on he has served as an agent and when he found that the amount was being misappropriated, he moved this Court for C.B.I. investigation in the matter.

During course of investigation, opposite party no.2 submitted all the documents, important papers,
certificates and one hard disk to the C.B.I. vide Production-cum-Seizure Memo dated 30.11.2017.

It is submitted that assertions made on behalf of petitioner that he had received the amount, is far from truth and he had re-channeled different account of the Company as per instruction of this petitioner and nothing was withdrawn for his personal use.

sentences.text: Considering the submissions of learned counsel and the fact that charge-sheet has already been submitted, the anticipatory bail application is allowed.

Hence, in the event of his arrest or surrender within a period of two weeks from the date of this order, the petitioner named above shall be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Court below, subject to the conditions laid down under section 438 (2) Cr. P.C.
One of the sureties shall be an income tax payee.
Petitioner shall surrender passport, if any, issued in his name before the trial Court while furnishing the Bail Bond.
I.A., if any, stands disposed of.
